title: POC scoping: open models shortlist - Verdant Health
summary: Discovery + POC scoping focused on open-model shortlist and benchmark criteria for Verdant Health clinical summarization use case. Primary goals: confirm success metrics (quality & hallucination thresholds), define workload sizing (concurrent requests, tokens/request), shortlist 3 open models to benchmark, agree on timeline for a 3-week POC, and call out security/compliance touches (HIPAA, VPC). Next steps: Redwood to share benchmark spreadsheet, SOW draft, and schedule benchmark run. Customer to provide redacted prompt set and data access details.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sofia from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. We also have Daniel from our SE team. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Priya Nair: Doing well, thanks. We have Marcus and Aisha on our side. Appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:12] Daniel Kim: quick intro from me — I'm the solutions engineer, I'll focus on benchmarks and infra questions.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Cool. To set expectations, we want a short POC to validate open models for clinical summarization — must handle PHI and support English + Spanish.
[00:29] Sofia Morales: Perfect, that's helpful. Priya, can you walk us through your success criteria? What will make this a win for Verdant?
[00:36] Priya Nair: Sure. Primary is quality — we want the summaries to match clinician judgments at least 85% of the time on our rubric, and hallucination rate under 5% on the test set. Latency is second — interactive workflows should be under 700ms tail for a 512-token response ideally, and cost should be reasonable — we have an internal threshold of roughly $X per thousand generated tokens but we can share exact numbers.
[01:05] Daniel Kim: Got it. When you say 85% on rubric, is that per-document or aggregate?
[01:09] Priya Nair: Aggregate, but we also care about worst-case — certain critical note types can't hallucinate.
[01:16] Aisha Gomez: Also need Spanish parity for common templates and medical terms.
[01:20] Sofia Morales: Understood. On the PHI front we'll treat this like an enterprise private deployment — Redwood Private or Dedicated is typically recommended for HIPAA workflows; we can run initial benchmarks on hosted if you prefer to accelerate.
[01:33] Marcus Lee: Prefer private from the start, but we can do initial model selection on hosted with redacted data if that helps speed things up.
[01:42] Daniel Kim: That works — we often do the model shortlist + synthetic/redacted prompts on hosted to get quick signal, then move to Dedicated or VPC for final runs.
[01:50] Sofia Morales: Let's talk workload sizing — what's your expected QPS and tokens per request?
[01:54] Priya Nair: Peak concurrency is ~8–10 concurrent users hitting summarization endpoint. Typical request is about 400 tokens in input and ~350 tokens generated, so ~750 tokens total. Daily volume is maybe 60k–100k generated tokens.
[02:10] Daniel Kim: Helpful — that points to focusing on models that can run efficiently with quantization and KV cache to reduce per-token cost. We'll size GPU types accordingly.
[02:20] Marcus Lee: Cost really matters; if a model is 2–3x cheaper but only slightly worse on domain accuracy, that might be acceptable. It's a tradeoff.
[02:28] Sofia Morales: Right, that's why we'll present a shortlist. For this POC we suggest benchmarking 3 open-model candidates: Llama 2 70B (quantized), Mistral Instruct (33B), and Falcon 40/180 family candidate (we can pick 40B as pragmatic). Each has tradeoffs: Llama 2 tends to be strong when finetuned, Mistral is efficient and good out-of-the-box, Falcon shows strong generation but can be larger.
[02:50] Priya Nair: Curious about multilingual — does Mistral handle Spanish well compared to Llama 2?
[02:55] Daniel Kim: In our internal tests Mistral tends to be solid for common Spanish phrases but Llama 2 70B with light finetune or prompt engineering often closes gaps. Falcon variable depending on the release and tokenizer — Spanish is okay but domain terms vary. We'll include targeted Spanish prompts in the benchmark suite.
[03:14] Aisha Gomez: What about hallucination controls? We need models that we can prompt or tune to reduce hallucinations.
[03:19] Daniel Kim: Good question. We evaluate hallucination via a hallucination rate on a curated set; techniques include instruction tuning, retrieval-augmented prompting, and constrained decoding. For the POC we can test plain generation, retrieval-augmented, and a safety-focused prompt template.
[03:33] Sofia Morales: We'll also measure ROUGE/F1 against your gold summaries, plus a human review pass for hallucination and criticality.
[03:40] Marcus Lee: Do you recommend a quantized runtime? We're sensitive to cost.
[03:44] Daniel Kim: Yes — Redwood's runtime supports int8/int4 quantization paths which often give 2-4x cost improvements with small quality degradation. We'll run both FP16 baseline and quantized variants in the benchmark matrix.
[03:56] Priya Nair: Timeline? How fast can we get results?
[03:58] Sofia Morales: Proposed 3-week POC: week 1 — confirm dataset + shortlist and run smoke tests on hosted with redacted prompts; week 2 — full benchmarks (quality, latency, cost) across the 3 models and variants; week 3 — final runs in Dedicated/VPC for the winner and SOW/next-phase discussion.
[04:15] Priya Nair: That aligns well. We'll need to see a rough SOW and the benchmark sheet.
[04:20] Sofia Morales: We'll share a benchmark spreadsheet and a POC SOW by Thursday (2026-05-21). The spreadsheet will include metric columns for ROUGE, F1, latency p50/p95/p99, hallucination rate, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:33] Aisha Gomez: On compliance — we need SOC2 + HIPAA attestation and audit logs. We also need to confirm KMS/HSM support for keys and whether logs can be routed to our SIEM.
[04:44] Daniel Kim: Redwood supports KMS integrations, audit logs export, and Dedicated/VPC that meet those requirements. We'll attach our security whitepaper and SOC2 summary.
[04:53] Marcus Lee: Any competitors we should be aware of? We evaluated Anthropic and OpenAI; OpenAI had better multilingual performance in earlier tests but cost was higher. We're also exploring some on-prem vendors.
[05:06] Sofia Morales: Noted. We'll include comparative notes but focus the POC on open models for cost control.
[05:12] Priya Nair: For benchmarks, we'll give you ~200 redacted notes in English and 80 in Spanish for the initial run. Is that enough?
[05:20] Daniel Kim: Yes, that's a good starting set to get statistically meaningful signals. We'll ask for a small critical subset for manual hallucination checks too.
[05:28] Aisha Gomez: Anything we need to provide aside from the notes? Roles/ops contact for VPC setup and redacted dataset upload.
[05:34] Sofia Morales: Yes — a secure S3 or transfer method for the redacted prompts, plus the contact who can approve a Dedicated trial if we proceed to that stage.
[05:42] Marcus Lee: I'll loop in infra.
[05:44] Sofia Morales: Great. Quick note on benchmarking config: we'll run each model at two temperature settings (0.0 and 0.7) and with/without retrieval to gauge hallucination sensitivity; measure latency on target GPU (A100/RTX equivalent) and simulated lower-end options for cost estimate.
[06:01] Daniel Kim: We'll also log token-level timings to help fine tune batching and KV cache settings.
[06:07] Priya Nair: Ok. For evaluation metrics, besides ROUGE/F1 and hallucination, can we add a clinical-accuracy binary metric that our clinicians will annotate?
[06:15] Sofia Morales: Absolutely, we'll add a column for clinician pass/fail. That will be helpful for the final decision.
[06:20] Aisha Gomez: Any known gotchas with Llama 2 licensing for a healthcare use-case?
[06:25] Daniel Kim: Llama 2's license has commercial terms but generally allowed; we'll include licensing notes. Mistral and Falcon have permissive licences too but always good to check legal — we'll attach a summary in the docs pack.
[06:36] Priya Nair: Good. One more question: can we run a small live demo later this week?
[06:40] Sofia Morales: Yes, we can schedule a 30-minute demo with an SE deep-dive where we run a smoke test on your redacted notes. How's Friday 10:00am PT?
[06:46] Marcus Lee: Works for us.
[06:48] Sofia Morales: Great. We'll send a calendar invite after the call.
[06:50] Aisha Gomez: Thanks.
[06:51] Sofia Morales: Quick recap: Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet, POC SOW draft, security docs/SOC2 summary, and schedule demo for Friday 2026-05-22 10:00am PT. Verdant to provide redacted prompt set, infra contact for VPC, and internal success rubric. We'll run benchmarks across Llama 2 70B (quantized), Mistral Instruct (33B), and Falcon 40B, plus quantized variants. Any final questions?
[07:12] Priya Nair: No, that's clear.
[07:14] Marcus Lee: Thanks everyone.
[07:16] Sofia Morales: Thanks — we'll follow up by Thursday. End call.
